data.name: Drift Into Eternity
data.detailed_description:
As the sole survivor of a distressed long-haul spaceship, you find yourself trapped within its falling apart remainings, struggling to maintain its vital functions
and coping with your own survival while a code-strangled AI tries to help you.

Explore, salvage, study and make a good use of the different modules of the ship to resolve this dreadful situation.

Inspired by our love for science-fiction classics and the survival genre, Drift Into Eternity presents you with a unique and difficult survival experience in first person
view. You'll have to quickly learn how to take advantage of the environment if you want to overcome the many dangers threatening the ship and your life.

Key Features:


  • Enter a cold, stark, silent ship, drifting in an asteroid field, its hull slowly being hammered by all sides, and its atmosphere being poisoned by its own toxic fuel released during the accident, while its vital functions die out one by one.
  • Explore and chart the ship for materials to repair its many devices, for food and water to prevent starvation, and try to keep your morale up to avoid fatal depression.
  • Repair the many damages slowly tearing apart the ship: close the breaches, repair its many devices, fight the many electrical fires, cleanse the corrosive and lethal atmosphere slowly infiltrating the hull.
  • Use the help of a sarcastic AI to gather the mandatory knowledge of your surroundings.
  • Study, craft, research and upgrade your tools to improve your chances of survival.
  • Take care of your diseases and wounds rapidly, if you don't want them to hinder your progression or put an end to it!
  • Minimal hand holding, you're the one trying to beat the game, we will only give hints on the very basic mechanics. Learning and progressing is all up to you.

This game is meant to be difficult and challenging for the players. You will struggle and fail often. But hold on tight, explore, observe and study... and maybe you'll find a way to survive each time a little longer!

The answer may be at the very end of the corridor!

data.short_description: Drift Into Eternity is a futuristic survival game in which you play a crewmember of a distressed spaceship, drifting in the middle of nowhere, so far from any civilisation that there is no hope of rescue. You're alone. Desperatly alone. Observe, Study, Explore... and maybe you'll find a way to survive.

reviews.review:
This game is an example of difficulty done poorly. It is hard, but in an incredibly boring manner.

It consists of wandering through a ship with 5 levels, each consisting of bland grey corridors that all basically look the same. You're supposed to fix things that break and keep yourself alive by looting in the process. To make this a challenge however, the maps displayed around the ship give next to zero informatron about where the key facilities are (such as oxygen production, temperature regulation, etc.).

For example, if you stand in a cold room for all of 30 seconds, you may receive 5 new diseases. To fix this, you should go to an infirmary. If only you knew where it is. Have fun trudging around each floor looking for one, only to forget where it is later should you need it because every part of the ship looks exactly the same. Perhaps you could hand draw a map or list of what each floor has, but I personally never felt motivation to put through such effort for this game.

There are no animations for anything. Not for the food and drink you have to spam throughout each day, not for the mysterious diseases you receive, not for the containers you look through to find more stupid crap. Nothing ever moves except for the particles of poison fuel gas (I forget the name), fire, doors, and your camera. 

There is nothing rewarding at all about staying alive. Parts of the ship will break that you didn't even know were there and fixing them consists of raising your tech-glove while suffering whatever malady is affecting the room until its gone. Oh, and you might get injured just for fixing them, because fuck you. The only motivation to continue living/playing that I can think of is just to be stubborn.

At the end of the day, as irritating it is to keep up my character's Morale stat by finding random items, the biggest challenge is keeping up my own morale to keep playing. I write this review after having played a round until I died and by the end I just wanted to die so I could play something else.

Now, the one positive note that I can leave is that the AI voice does have a few good lines that I appreciate. Hopefully they will help you bear through the silence broken only by your footsteps. I really do like the concept of what this game should be, but the execution is just terrible at this point. Perhaps this game will get better, but I'm going to spend my time with other games for now.
